analyst_note: Hormuz Day 71; Naval Blockade Day 29; Project Freedom Pause Day 5; WPA Day 11 Past Statutory Deadline. vibe.rationale: Vibe holds at 4 — unchanged from Saturday. Sunday's quietude prevents a downgrade but delivers nothing to justify an upgrade. Three compounding forces from yesterday's brief remain unresolved and have deepened: Iran's non-response is now 96+ hours past the 48-hour window with no indication of imminent transmission through the Pakistan channel; Trump's 'one big glow' nuclear threat language is now 24 hours old without White House, State Department, or CENTCOM clarification, meaning it has been allowed to stand as official US posture; and the overnight naval exchange from Saturday (US self-defense strikes in the Strait during Project Freedom pause) adds an unresolved escalation precedent that grows more significant with each quiet day the pause nominally holds. The structural deal logic that has prevented a lower score remains intact: the Pakistan intermediary role has not been formally suspended, Iran's answer is formally 'not yet' rather than 'no,' and no IRGC destructive cyberattack has materialized through Day 7 post-Project Freedom launch. Triple-convergence week opening Monday is a source of both risk and potential clarity: Warsh's confirmation — nearly certain at 54-46 — removes one variable; but the compressed timeline (Warsh vote + Powell expiry + Reconciliation deadline all within four days) creates conditions where a single negative surprise in the Iran deal track could cascade through multiple domestic policy mechanisms simultaneously. Vibe 4: deal track suspended in amber, nuclear rhetoric unretracted, oil frozen above $100 until Monday price discovery, and PNW fire season accelerating ahead of calendar.

items.headline: Iran Non-Response Now 96+ Hours: MOU Window Four Days Overdue; Pakistan Channel Active But Silent; No Sunday Transmission Confirmed
items.summary: Iran has not transmitted a formal response to the 14-point MOU framework through the Pakistan back-channel as of Sunday evening, May 10 — now more than 96 hours past the 48-hour response window that expired Thursday May 8. The pattern of non-response has become the dominant diplomatic signal of the crisis: each passing day without a formal answer raises the domestic political cost inside Iran of eventually accepting, as the MOU is now publicly framed in Iranian political discourse as an American demand list delivered under nuclear coercion. Iran's Foreign Ministry remains in 'review' status; parliament has characterized the framework as an 'American wish list'; the Expediency Council has demanded reparations; and the IRGC has offered no public softening. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's role as intermediary has not been formally suspended — Pakistan's expressed hope for a deal 'soon' (May 6) remains the last direct positive signal from the channel — but Sunday delivered no new Pakistan Foreign Ministry statement confirming receipt of a formal Iranian response. The US operational posture is unchanged: Project Freedom remains paused (Pause Day 5), the naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in full effect, ~1,600 vessels remain stranded in regional waters, and approximately 23,000 sailors remain at sea. Trump's Truth Social and public comment streams produced no new Iran deal statement on Sunday. The absence of a 'deal collapse' announcement — from any party — is the sole structural positive of Sunday's diplomatic environment. The Pakistan channel's silence over a weekend period is not definitively negative, as formal diplomatic transmission has historically lagged across weekend windows; Monday's opening will be the first business-day test of whether the channel produces a response.

items.headline: Trump 'One Big Glow' Nuclear Threat Stands Unretracted at 24 Hours; No White House / State / CENTCOM Clarification Issued; Strategic Damage to Deal Space Calcifying
items.summary: Twenty-four hours after President Trump issued the most explicit nuclear-adjacent threat language of the 71-day crisis — 'If there's no ceasefire, you're not going to have to know. You're just going to have to look at one big glow coming out of Iran. And they better sign their agreement fast' — no White House, State Department, or CENTCOM clarification, correction, or contextual statement has been issued. The absence of clarification allows the statement to stand as the operative US posture: an explicit nuclear threat delivered to a nation currently holding the MOU unsigned. The strategic damage compounds with time: each day the statement stands unaddressed, it becomes harder for any Iranian political faction to frame acceptance of the MOU as a product of negotiation rather than capitulation under nuclear duress. Iran's Expediency Council, parliament, and IRGC all face domestic audiences with no tolerance for a deal publicly characterized as yielding to nuclear blackmail. The Trump-Putin call — in which Trump claimed 'the war is very complete, pretty much' — remains the last substantive diplomatic signal of the weekend, and no Russian Foreign Ministry or Kremlin readout of that call has been made public with operational detail. No resumption of Project Freedom was announced Sunday. The pause holds; the rhetoric escalates.

items.headline: Markets Closed Sunday; Brent Frozen at $101.73; Monday Futures Open Is First Price Discovery for Weekend Signals; EIA Forecasts Brent Q2 Peak at $115 If Deal Fails
items.summary: No new oil price data is available for Sunday May 10 — global commodity markets and US equity markets are closed. Brent crude's last confirmed close is $101.73 (May 8), approximately 49% above the pre-war baseline of ~$68; WTI's last confirmed close is $94.81 (May 7) with estimates of $95–97 on May 8–9. Monday's electronic futures open — approximately 6 PM ET Sunday — will be the first market pricing event incorporating the weekend's accumulated signals: Trump's 'one big glow' nuclear threat, the overnight naval exchange during Project Freedom pause, and Iran's continued non-response now at 96+ hours past the window. The directional risk is asymmetric: these signals are collectively oil-price-positive (supply-disruption risk premium) and none of the weekend's events constitutes a deal-positive signal that would drive a downward move. The US Energy Information Administration's Short-Term Energy Outlook projects Brent to peak at approximately $115/barrel in Q2 2026 if the Strait disruption persists — the scenario consistent with a failed deal or prolonged Project Freedom resumption. The deal-acceptance scenario remains operative as a downside oil case: formal Iranian MOU acceptance would likely drive a 15–20% crude price decline over 4–6 weeks as supply restoration expectations build. National average gas prices remain above $4.50 per gallon (AAA), lagging any crude price move by 2–4 weeks — meaning consumers would not see relief for weeks even if a deal closed Monday. Brent remains approximately 49% above pre-war baseline; WTI approximately 40% above pre-war baseline.

items.headline: Triple-Convergence Week Opens Monday: Warsh Vote 5:30 PM ET, Powell Expiry May 15, Reconciliation Deadline May 15; Five Days of Simultaneous Institutional Transition
items.summary: Monday May 11 opens the most compressed week of domestic institutional convergence of the current Congress. Three simultaneous timelines reach resolution or deadline between May 11–15: (1) Kevin Warsh's Senate floor vote, confirmed for 5:30 PM ET Monday, at which point Warsh is expected to be confirmed by approximately 54-46 or better — all 53 Senate Republicans plus Senator John Fetterman (D-PA), who has indicated support; (2) Jerome Powell's term as Federal Reserve Chair expires May 15 — the first involuntary term expiry of a sitting Fed chair since the post-WWII era; (3) Reconciliation 2.0 committee submission deadline May 15, requiring all designated Senate committees to transmit their measures to the Budget Committee. The first wholly partisan committee vote on a Fed chair nominee in history (13-0 Republican, 11-0 Democrat) sets the template for what is now a structurally politicized Federal Reserve. Warsh inherits a policy environment defined by an external oil shock entirely outside domestic monetary tools: WTI ~$95–97 (40% above pre-war baseline), Brent $101.73 (49% above baseline), and a war-driven inflation premium that rate policy cannot address. His first FOMC meeting is expected June 16. Reconciliation 2.0 status: Senate Homeland Security and Judiciary committees released $72B ICE/Border Patrol text May 4 (CBO scored); Finance, Armed Services, and other designated committees face the May 15 deadline. Trump's self-imposed completion deadline for the full reconciliation package is June 1.

items.headline: CISA Day 7: No Confirmed Destructive IRGC Attack; Sunday Peak Weekend Risk Window; Naval Exchange Saturday Is Unresolved Trigger; CI Fortify Operative
items.summary: Seven days after Project Freedom launched (May 4), CISA has confirmed no IRGC-affiliated or Handala-attributed destructive cyberattack on US critical infrastructure. CISA has issued no updated advisory beyond AA26-097A (April 7, 2026), which warned of CyberAv3ngers (IRGC Cyber Electronic Command affiliate) exploitation of programmable logic controllers across Government Services, Water and Wastewater, and Energy sectors. CI Fortify remains operative; FINRA's financial-sector alert and NERC's active grid monitoring remain in effect. Sunday represents the maximum risk point of the weekend window: minimum IT security staffing, slower incident response capacity, and the unresolved context of Saturday's naval exchange in the Strait — which IRGC cyber doctrine could internally frame as operational justification for retaliatory cyber action against US infrastructure even during the nominal Project Freedom pause. Three compounding risk factors are simultaneously active as of Sunday evening: (1) peak weekend staffing reduction; (2) an unacknowledged Saturday kinetic exchange that has not produced an IRGC statement on their perception of the ceasefire's status; (3) Iran's non-response to the MOU at 96+ hours creates an internal IRGC calculus question — continued patience vs. pressure operations to strengthen Tehran's negotiating hand. The sustained 7-day absence of a destructive attack through two weekend periods is the most significant positive infrastructure signal of the crisis. CISA's threat posture: prior to the crisis, Iran conducted the March 2026 Handala-Stryker operation (200,000 devices wiped across 79 countries) and the April 1 Chime Financial attack, establishing the operational template and willingness to strike critical infrastructure. The CI Fortify framework represents the US defensive response architecture. Any new CISA emergency directive, FBI/IC3 flash, or private-sector incident report over the Sunday-Monday transition constitutes a priority signal.

items.headline: Oregon Fire Season Day 3: Portland Confirms 90°F Sunday; No Red Flag Warning; Congressional Democrats Flag Federal Response Capacity Gap; 22 Days to East Cascades Above-Normal Onset
items.summary: Oregon's 2026 fire season (declared effective May 8) is now in its third active day. Portland's forecast 90°F high was reached on Sunday May 10 — the first 90-degree day of May, occurring ahead of the historical average and at the precise threshold associated with accelerated soil moisture depletion and fine-fuel curing in the Columbia Gorge and east of the Cascades. No National Weather Service Portland red flag warning was issued for Sunday's heat event; wind conditions did not achieve the concurrent threshold required for a formal watch/warning designation. Oregon fire agencies maintain approximately 700 wildland firefighters and 300 fire trucks in protective position for 16 million Oregon acres, supplemented by 300+ local fire departments and federal and tribal wildland firefighters. The structural risk environment for the 2026 season is defined by Oregon's 2025–2026 winter — tied with 1934 as the warmest on record — producing dangerously low snowpack and compressing the fine-fuel curing timeline into an unusually early May window. June 1 above-normal east Cascades fire risk onset: 22 days away. Oregon's congressional Democrats (Reps. Bonamici, Hoyle, Salinas, Blumenauer, Chavez-DeRoemer) formally raised concerns May 7 about degraded federal wildfire response capacity — specifically DOGE-related reductions to Forest Service Region 6, including elimination of fire science research positions and reduced pre-positioning capability — in letters to Interior and Agriculture secretaries. Washington DNR burn restrictions and Portland metro burn bans remain in effect. AccuWeather projects 5.5 million acres burned nationally in 2026.

items.headline: WPA Day 11: Constitutional Accountability Gap Broadens Silently; Triple-Convergence Week Opens Monday; No War-Authorization Scheduling Announced; Senate Recess Ends Monday
items.summary: Today is WPA Day 11 past the April 29 statutory deadline under the War Powers Resolution — the longest the current administration has operated without congressional authorization since Project Freedom launched May 4. The constitutional accountability gap is broadening daily: 36 hours of offensive operations conducted May 4–5 without congressional authorization, plus the ongoing naval blockade and self-defense strikes during the pause, accumulate without a floor vote or authorization resolution. Senate Republicans have rejected six Democratic war-powers resolutions since the crisis began; no seventh has been scheduled. Senate leadership has announced no war-authorization floor scheduling for triple-convergence week, suggesting the WPA accountability question remains politically tabled while the deal window is open. The Trump administration's legal posture — that the War Powers Resolution clock stopped when the president declared hostilities 'effectively ended' via cease-fire and Project Freedom pause — remains the operative interpretation, contested in academic and advocacy circles but not litigated. Triple-convergence week opens Monday May 11 with the Warsh floor vote at 5:30 PM ET, representing the most watched procedural event of the week. Warsh's path to confirmation is solid (53 Republican votes + Fetterman), but any procedural hold, floor motion to delay, or surprise defection would be a market-moving event. The Reconciliation 2.0 May 15 deadline creates parallel pressure: Finance, Armed Services, and other designated committees must complete measures in the same week as the Warsh vote and Powell expiry. Alabama and Tennessee redistricting special sessions continue; no ACLU or NAACP LDF legal challenge has been filed; the November 2026 map-lock window is approximately 4.5 months and narrowing.

items.headline: Portland Hits 90°F Sunday; First Day Over 90 in May; Fire Season Day 3 Active; No Red Flag Warning; Federal Response Capacity Concerns Filed; 22 Days to Above-Normal East Cascades
items.summary: Portland confirmed a high of approximately 90°F on Sunday May 10 — the first 90-degree day of the 2026 May period, occurring ahead of the historical average and as forecast. The threshold is significant for fire behavior: 90°F with low relative humidity accelerates soil moisture depletion and advances fine-fuel curing in the Columbia Gorge and east of the Cascades — the region most at risk for early-season fire behavior ahead of the June 1 above-normal onset. No National Weather Service Portland red flag warning was issued for Sunday's heat event; concurrent east-gradient wind development in the Gorge did not reach the threshold for a formal watch. Oregon's fire season (declared May 8, now Day 3) remains in its pre-peak protective posture: ODF permitting restrictions and patrol requirements operative; 700 wildland firefighters and 300 fire trucks in position; state resources supplemented by federal and tribal responders. Oregon's congressional Democrats — Reps. Bonamici, Hoyle, Salinas, Blumenauer, and Chavez-DeRoemer — filed formal concerns May 7 with USDA and Interior secretaries about reduced federal wildfire response capacity under DOGE cuts to Forest Service Region 6, specifically the elimination of fire science research positions and reduced pre-positioning resources. The concern is structural: the 2026 fire season is projected as among the worst in Oregon history (2025–2026 winter tied warmest on record; snowpack dangerously low), and federal response capacity has been degraded heading into it. Portland metro and BLM Oregon-Washington burn bans remain in effect. June 1 above-normal east Cascades onset: 22 days. Brent crude's freeze at $101.73 continues to delay PNW consumer pump price relief by at minimum two weeks from any crude price movement.

items.headline: PNW Measles: OR ~20 Confirmed (Last Published April 22); WA 40+; Wastewater Surveillance Active; OHA Count Expected Monday-Tuesday; Vaccination Window Narrowing to 5 Weeks
items.summary: No new Oregon Health Authority measles case count was published Sunday May 10. The most recent published Oregon figure remains approximately 20 confirmed cases as of April 22, 2026, with OHA officials consistently acknowledging substantial suspected underreporting. OHA's wastewater surveillance dashboard continues to detect measles viral concentrations in counties with no confirmed cases — a structurally leading indicator of geographically distributed transmission outpacing case-finding capacity. Washington State holds at 40+ confirmed cases year-to-date across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in formal outbreak status. The US national total as of April 30, 2026 stood at 1,814 confirmed cases across 37 jurisdictions. Structural transmission drivers are unchanged: below-threshold MMR vaccination coverage pockets in both states, DOGE-related CDC response capacity constraints, and active school-year community spread dynamics. The school-year vaccination catch-up window — most PNW districts close mid-to-late June — is now approximately 5 weeks and narrowing. The combined Oregon-Washington confirmed count of 60+ with acknowledged undercounting represents the highest bi-state measles burden in at least a generation. The next OHA case count update is expected Monday May 11 or Tuesday May 12, consistent with weekday publishing cadence; the published count is expected to show material increase from the April 22 figure given the sustained wastewater detection pattern in non-reporting counties.
